title: Serre affineness criterion for algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Assume $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, meaning that every open cover has a finite subcover and the diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Modules and quasi-coherence are on the small etale ringed site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Write $H^q(X,M)=R^q\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{et}},M)$ for cohomology of the underlying additive sheaf [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. If $H^1(X,F)=0$ for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$, then $X$ is represented by an affine scheme.

source.place: Tag 07V6, proposition-vanishing-affine, with the precise hypothesis H^1=0 in situation-vanishing (Tag 07UY).

proof.text: Put $A=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. By [lem-sfb-space-acyclic-affinization-geometry], the absolute canonical map $p:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ exists, is separated, and is universally injective. All its hypotheses are the assumptions of the item. Choose a disjoint-affine etale atlas by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover] and a finite subatlas by [lem-a1-space-finite-affine-subatlas]. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum], this finite disjoint union is an affine scheme $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$. Denote its surjective etale map by $\varphi:U\to X$.

source.place: Tag 07V6, first sentence and Tags 07V4, 07V5; Tag 03H6 affine atlas construction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-affine-etale-polynomial-generators] with $f=p$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Separatedness and the affine surjective etale chart were established in step 1. Obtain a surjection $e:P=\mathcal O_X[z_1,\ldots,z_m]\twoheadrightarrow\varphi_*\mathcal O_U$ with quasi-coherent kernel $K$. The hypothesis gives $H^1(X,K)=0$. The long exact sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact], applied to the underlying additive sheaves of $0\to K\to P\to\varphi_*\mathcal O_U\to0$, makes $\Gamma(X,P)\to\Gamma(X,\varphi_*\mathcal O_U)=B$ surjective. The abelian sheaf category has enough injectives and its global-sections functor is left exact by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology].

source.place: Tag 07V6, polynomial surjection and vanishing of H^1 of its kernel.

proof.text: The underlying additive sheaf of $P$ is the filtered colimit of its finite sums of monomial summands $\mathcal O_X$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-cohomology-filtered-colimit] at $q=0$. Sections of each finite sum are the corresponding finite sum of $A$, since finite sums of abelian sheaves are finite products and sections preserve products. Thus every section of $P$ is a finite polynomial with coefficients in $A$, and multiplication sends the monomial summands to their products. Therefore $\Gamma(X,P)=A[z_1,\ldots,z_m]$ as rings. The surjection in step 2 shows that $B$ is generated as an $A$-algebra by the finite tuple $(g_i)$.

source.place: Tag 07V6, displayed global-sections polynomial ring; Tag 073E with p=0.

proof.text: Regard $X$ as an algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ through $X\to S\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]: on all schemes $T$ put $X'(T)=\coprod_{a:T\to S}X(T\xrightarrow{a}S)$. This is an fppf sheaf with representable diagonal, and its representable surjective etale scheme charts are those of $X$. The assignment $X\mapsto(X',X'\to h_S)$ is an equivalence between algebraic spaces over $S$ and algebraic spaces over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with a map to $h_S$. It keeps fibre products, field-valued points, the atlas topology and the small etale ringed site (Stacks, Spaces, Tag 04SG). In this sense $p$ is a morphism of algebraic spaces over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, as in the construction of Tag 05Z1. The nodes below that are stated over a base scheme are applied with base $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. The scheme morphism $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is locally of finite type: the single affine cover $U$ has finitely generated coordinate algebra, exactly the definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test] with target chart the identity of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and source chart $U\to X$; it gives local finite type of $p$. By universal injectivity, each field fibre of $p$ has at most one point, hence is discrete (its only possible subsets are empty and the whole space). Now [lem-sfb-space-discrete-fibres-locally-quasifinite] gives local quasi-finiteness of $p$.

source.place: Tag 07V6, B finite type and application of Tag 06RW. Change of base scheme to Spec Z: spaces.tex Tag 04SG (lemma-category-of-spaces-over-smaller-base-scheme); spaces-properties.tex Tag 05Z1.

proof.text: The separated locally quasi-finite morphism $p$ has scheme target. Apply [lem-a1-separated-locally-qf-space-representable] to obtain a scheme $Z$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ representing $X'$. Its point space is quasi-compact because it is the point space of $X$. For each quasi-coherent Zariski ideal $I\subseteq\mathcal O_Z$, its associated etale module $I_{\mathrm{et}}$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], so $H^1(Z_{\mathrm{et}},I_{\mathrm{et}})=0$ by the original hypothesis transported along the representing isomorphism. The comparison [lem-sc-etale-zariski-qcoh-comparison] at $q=1$ gives $H^1(Z,I)=0$ in scheme module cohomology. Hence [lem-pqf-quasicompact-h1-zero] applies and makes $Z$ affine. This proves the required representability by an affine scheme. The transported structural map $Z\to S$ is a scheme morphism: evaluate the natural transformation $h_Z\simeq X'\to h_S$ at $\mathrm{id}_Z$; naturality identifies every component with composition by that map. By the equivalence recalled in step 4 [def-trf-algebraic-space], $h_Z$ with this map to $h_S$ corresponds to $X$, so the $S$-scheme $Z$ represents $X$ as an algebraic space over $S$.

source.place: Tag 07V6, final two sentences; Tag 03XX representability and Tag 01XF scheme criterion. Return to the base S: spaces.tex Tag 04SG.
